summary: Final multi-tenant security retest. Required regression (test_multitenant + test_tenancy + test_iter12_mt_p0, -n 0): 46/46 pass. New file test_iter13_mt_final.py: 10/11 pass. It explicitly covers: eFactura disconnect on a non-demo tenant (all 5 token fields are unset, the other tenant and demo are untouched). TenantCollection: $set, $unset, $rename (both directions), update_many, find_one_and_update with $currentDate, and upsert all keep tenant_id/branch_id. Pipeline updates return 400. 10 raw unscoped methods raise AttributeError. Missing scope returns 503 on find. OAuth callback: empty or missing state, and error-only calls, redirect to oauth=error with 0 new logs and no change to any config. A generic exception (non-Fernet secret raises InvalidToken) redirects instead of returning 500, logs only to its own tenant, and state replay is rejected. Tenant SUSPENDED/EXPIRED and branch INACTIVE block me, refresh, login, CRUD, dashboard and settings; reactivating restores access. SUPERADMIN cannot suspend its own context tenant. Cross-tenant: CRUD by id returns 404, vehicle_count aggregate, cash-register aggregate and dashboard are isolated. VIN uniqueness is per tenant and a foreign client_id is rejected. Branch quota is enforced. A tenant admin cannot edit or delete the SUPERADMIN. Auth: httpOnly Secure cookies; CORS uses an explicit origin with credentials and rejects foreign origins. UI: Superadmin tenant creation works; dashboard scrollWidth is 390 at 390px and 768 at 768px; Superadmin page is 390 at 390px; demo admin sees platform-access-denied. No page errors. No P0 multi-tenant bypass found. The single failure is minor hardening: an upsert with no scope raises TypeError (500) instead of 503. It still fails closed and nothing is written.

minor.issue: When there is no tenant scope, the upsert branch does scope['tenant_id'] on None and raises TypeError (HTTP 500) instead of HTTPException 503. It fails closed and no write happens, but the error is not clean. Fix: call _scope_filter(query) first, or check for scope before building $setOnInsert.

action_items: Optional/minor: make the no-scope upsert path in TenantCollection raise 503 instead of TypeError (test_tenantcollection_update_operators asserts this).
critical_code_review_comments: TenantCollection.aggregate only prepends $match on the base collection. $lookup, $unionWith, $graphLookup, $out and $merge stages can read or write other collections unscoped. Current pipelines (clients vehicle_count, cash-register, final-inspection inspectors) do not use them. Consider rejecting these stages in TenantCollection.aggregate to fail closed in future.
/auth/refresh does not compare the refresh token's tenant_id/branch_id claims with the user doc. The new access token is rebuilt from the DB, so this is low risk.
The access token is still returned in the JSON body and kept in localStorage alongside httpOnly cookies (an existing design choice that weakens XSS protection).

success_rate.backend: 98% (56/57: 46/46 regression + 10/11 new; the 1 failure is minor hardening)

TEMP-ui13-tenant was created via the UI and deleted. cleanup_temp_check.py shows 0 TEMP/TEST tenants, branches, users, counters, clients, payments, efactura_config, efactura_logs and cron_errors left. UI: the dashboard table min-w-[480px] sits inside an overflow-x-auto wrapper, so page scrollWidth stays 390.
rca of the issue: Minor: in TenantCollection.update_one/find_one_and_update, the upsert block reads current_scope() and indexes it before _scope_filter() runs, so a missing scope raises TypeError rather than the intended 503.
